contract.purpose: Reverse-lookup registry of open questions. Read in the direction question -> axis -> intervention -> observation unit -> is there an instrument, so that 'we have no instrument for this' is an answer the repository can give instead of a gap nobody notices.
contract.rule: status belongs to the CLAIM, never to an implementation. Shipping a mitigation does not close a question; only closure_criteria being met does. `class-aware coverage is implemented` is not an answer to `is item breadth a bottleneck`.
contract.missing_instrument_is_an_answer: When required_instrument is not in context/measurements.json, the honest response to the question is 'insufficient evidence, and here is the intervention that would produce it' -- not a hedge assembled from instruments that were conditioned on something else.

questions.question: Does MAX_POOL_ITEMS_EVALUATED = 10 discard items that would have been placed?
questions.intervention: cap 20 on the same paired permutation design, plus a second multiset; for the per-item question, shadow evaluation of skipped items
questions.required_variation: same multiset and arrival order across arms; at least 2 multisets to avoid a single-stream result
questions.missing_instrument: For the fixed cap: none, it is measured. For 'which excluded item was lost' and for an adaptive rule: still nothing -- an item that never entered the search has nothing computed about it, so shadow evaluation of skipped items remains unbuilt.
questions.why_unobserved: Only the per-item half is unobserved now. Whether a bigger cap helps has been measured; which specific excluded item was lost still cannot be recovered from any log, because an item that never entered the search has nothing computed about it.
questions.rationale: At pool 40 the agent evaluates 25% of visible items. Merely REALLOCATING the same 10 slots (class-aware coverage) moved placed 10.67 -> 17.00 and priority C1 0% -> 81.2%, which is the largest single effect in the ledger. The cap itself has never been varied because it is a source constant with no override -- the absence of a knob, not a judgement, is why this was never tested. [2026-08-02 UPDATED after merging the stride branch: this question was filed as fully open because the registry was built against a checkout that predated the env-isation. The cap had already been made a knob (d69bc36) and swept.]
closure_criteria: DONE for the fixed-cap form: two sources measured, effect source-dependent
OPEN if pursued as a conditional/adaptive cap: needs a difficulty signal measurable online, then a paired test of the rule rather than the constant
questions.answer_so_far: NO, not as an unconditional intervention. Paired permutation on TWO sources: 000 gave +3.125 placed (8/0/0, two-sided p = 0.0078) but 001 gave -0.125 (3 wins / 4 losses / 1 tie, p = 1.0). Pooled +1.500, 11/4/1, p = 0.1185 -- not established. MAX_POOL_ITEMS_EVALUATED stays 10. Untested candidate mechanism: the cap binds only where the pool is hard to place from (base placed 12.750 on 000 versus 16.625 on 001), which would make it a conditional intervention rather than a default.

questions.question: Does a real graded state value V(sigma(s')) improve selection?
questions.intervention: implement a graded estimator and use it to act; there is currently nothing to turn on
questions.required_variation: episode-level arms across >= 5 configs with repeats sized against the per-config variance in MEASUREMENT_AUDIT F3
questions.missing_instrument: Schema-v4 H3 teachers now provide per-axis physical afterstate continuation targets and a run-held-out offline estimator audit. What remains missing is a representation that beats action-only and a switchable episode policy; the current afterstate summary does neither.
questions.rationale: Schema-v4 closes the teacher-target gap: continuation gain subtracts the child state's H0 outcome from its reachable H3 leaves. Actions run 31595519595 verified 67/67 paired child tensors. Across five run-held-out splits, afterstate fill was 21/22 versus action-only 17/22 and permuted maximum 13/22; paired 4 wins / 18 ties / 0 losses gives exact p=0.125 because only four rows disagree. Surface does not transfer (13/26, and 2/13/11 versus immediate score, p=0.02246). A fill-only state hypothesis is now justified, but incremental value and an acting intervention remain unestablished.
closure_criteria: a graded estimator exists and is switchable
an episode-level arm measured with repeats that exceed the config variance

questions.question: Does the bounded128 adoption transfer to a second real Task A case?
questions.intervention: run the adopted arm against base on a second bundled or supplied Task A case
questions.required_variation: >= 3 repeats per arm; the offline order is deterministic but the physical outcome is a range (25-26 on case 000)
questions.missing_instrument: none -- the instrument exists, only the case is missing. Source 001 is a synthetic conversion and was deliberately dropped from the adoption matrix.
questions.rationale: The adoption rests on n=1 case. The AABB cache is the standing precedent that a genuine starvation fix can be strongly positive on one config and strongly negative on another.
closure_criteria: one real non-synthetic Task A case measured with >= 3 repeats per arm

questions.question: What effect size can the Task B regression guard actually resolve?
questions.intervention: rebuild reports/benchmarks/baseline.json with repeats and a machine fingerprint; make same-machine A/B the procedure instead of comparison to a stored constant
questions.required_variation: >= 3 repeats per config, >= 5 on configs measured as volatile
questions.missing_instrument: none structurally; the baseline itself is the defective part (n=1, foreign machine, no fingerprint)
questions.rationale: Measured 2026-08-02: an identical binary on an identical box returns 13, 17, 18 placed on b000-k40. The guard's own contract asks for unexplained drops to be rejected, which it cannot support. Three of five configs were perfectly stable, so this is config-specific, and the two volatile ones are exactly those carrying the aabb-cache-guard-mixed conclusion.
closure_criteria: the guard states a minimum resolvable effect size
same-machine A/B documented as the procedure

questions.question: Would a risk-on dry run propose better orders than the risk-off one?
questions.intervention: pass risk_lambda into DryRunEvaluator as a comparison arm
questions.missing_instrument: none -- it needs a new arm, not a new instrument
questions.rationale: Closed by Actions run 31569837492: default versus risk_on, both bundled Task A cases, three repeats per arm. Risk-on improved a001 by +1 placed but regressed a000 by 6 placed and 7.35 fill on the means. It also evaluated fewer orders (42.0 versus 53.7 on a000; 76.3 versus 91.0 on a001) at comparable optimization time. The proposal-recall loss dominates; keep ADR-003 risk-off default.
closure_criteria: fingerprint re-stamped and Task A numbers re-measured

questions.question: Is the Ranker's functional form defensible, or merely unexamined?
questions.intervention: expose the score weights as knobs and sweep them
questions.required_variation: episode arms with repeats above the config variance
questions.missing_instrument: The weights are still source literals with no knob, so the FORM cannot be swept. What now exists is a long-horizon paired label to score a form against: build_branch_labels.py measured within-step concordance between immediate Q and final placed at 0.267 against a chance level of 0.500, on 15 decided pairs from one episode -- suggestive, not established.
questions.rationale: The volume term is known to be a dead vote within an item, and the risk work added a correction on top of the existing form without ever testing the form. Same structural pattern as the item cap: no knob, so no hypothesis. [2026-08-02: first long-horizon evidence that the ordering may be actively wrong rather than merely unexamined, which raises the value of exposing the weights.]
closure_criteria: at least one sweep measured at episode level

questions.question: What should the agent return when no candidate is acceptable?
questions.intervention: none available -- the fixed protocol fallback has no knob
questions.missing_instrument: analyze_terminal_failures is a post-mortem over deaths; it has no counterfactual and its denominator is deaths, not attempts. Two designed replacements (deadline-reserved rescue, cross-step incumbent) were both rejected, and neither was a variation of the fallback itself.
questions.rationale: transport_invalid is the leading death channel at 45% of endings and the audited fatal actions fail the agent's own static check, i.e. they are the fallback firing, not the search failing.
closure_criteria: measured against the current one at episode level
